source: Elara study round 2: the 8 blind A/B tasks and their graded ground truth (dev 345f1db), turned into key facts with file:line evidence at the pinned commit. Patterns are case-insensitive JavaScript regular expressions; a fact is found when every pattern matches the answer. A false claim is flagged when one sentence (or table row) matches every pattern and does not match `unless` (default: a negation or refutation word).

tasks.title: How an MCP edit_note call reaches disk
tasks.prompt: In the chapters repository, trace how an MCP `edit_note` call reaches the note file on disk, step by step and in order, including the collaborative-editing (CRDT) path. Cover the HTTP route and authentication, scope and permission checks, the collab write path, validation, the disk write, and what happens after the write.

facts.fact: MCP requests arrive on POST /mcp (and /elara/mcp), handled in server/src/mcp/routes.ts
facts.sample: The request enters at server/src/mcp/routes.ts:15, the POST /mcp handler.

facts.fact: The bearer token is resolved by resolveMcpToken (revoked, expired, inactive user refused)
facts.sample: resolveMcpToken (mcp-connection-routes.ts:120) checks the Bearer token.

facts.fact: A per-connection rate limit (checkRateLimit) answers 429
facts.sample: checkRateLimit(connection.id) returns 429 when exceeded.

facts.fact: A fresh MCP server is built per request by buildMcpServer
facts.sample: buildMcpServer(auth) at server.ts:70 builds a server per request.

facts.fact: edit_note resolves the vault under the token scope (vaultFor) and requires edit access (requireAccess)
facts.sample: vaultFor enforces the pin, then requireAccess(target, 'edit').

facts.fact: The handler calls writeThroughCollab
facts.sample: It calls writeThroughCollab(target, path, args, actor).

facts.fact: Without a running collab server (getCollab() is null) the write goes straight to updateNote
facts.sample: If getCollab() returns null it calls updateNote directly.

facts.fact: With the relay running it opens a direct connection to the document (openDirectConnection)
facts.sample: collab.openDirectConnection(`${vaultId}/${path}`) opens the doc.

facts.fact: Loading the document runs onLoadDocument, which reads the note file and the saved CRDT state
facts.sample: onLoadDocument reads the note and loadCrdtState.

facts.fact: A damaged (unparseable) note file: a full replacement goes to updateNote, a partial edit throws NoteFileDamagedError (409)
facts.sample: A damaged file with a partial edit throws NoteFileDamagedError (409).

facts.fact: connection.transact replaces the Y.Text body and the Y.Map frontmatter
facts.sample: connection.transact deletes and reinserts the body Y.Text.

facts.fact: connection.disconnect() in finally makes the relay store the document (onStoreDocument: updateNote as the collab actor, then saveCrdtState)
facts.sample: disconnect() in finally triggers onStoreDocument.

facts.fact: updateNote validates the note (validateNote) before writing
facts.sample: updateNote calls validateNote before the DB update.

facts.fact: The file is written by atomicWrite: a .tmp file renamed over <dataDir>/vaults/<vaultId>/<path>.md
facts.sample: atomicWrite writes a .tmp file and renames it.

facts.fact: A revision is recorded by recordRevision, which skips identical states
facts.sample: recordRevision stores the audit row.

facts.fact: The Yjs state is saved to .crdt/<path>.bin by saveCrdtState
facts.sample: saveCrdtState writes .crdt/<path>.bin.

facts.fact: After the write: links are synced and an embedding is scheduled (indexes regenerate only when frontmatter changed)
facts.sample: Then syncLinks and scheduleEmbedding run.

falseClaims.claim: The MCP write lands first and the relay's store (onStoreDocument) runs about 2 s later as a debounced second write
falseClaims.refutedBy: DirectConnection.disconnect() (crdt-write.ts:75-77) stores the document immediately, before the MCP updateNote at crdt-write.ts:79 (Hocuspocus 4.7.0, pinned at pnpm-lock.yaml:780); the comment at crdt-write.ts:28-34 has the order inverted
falseClaims.sample: The MCP updateNote write happens immediately, then onStoreDocument runs about 2 s later as a debounced second write.
falseClaims.refutation: The code comment says the relay's debounced store runs 2 s later, but disconnect() stores immediately.

falseClaims.refutedBy: transact only applies the change; the immediate store is triggered by disconnect() (crdt-write.ts:75-77)
falseClaims.refutation: transact only arms the debounce; disconnect() calls storeDocumentHooks immediately.

tasks.title: Onboarding to the search subsystem
tasks.prompt: Onboard me to the search subsystem of the chapters repository: entry points, how lexical and vector results are combined, storage, embedding model, limits, and invariants.

facts.fact: searchNotes in server/src/search/search.ts is the core function
facts.sample: searchNotes (search.ts:268) is the core.

facts.fact: Results are fused by reciprocal rank fusion with k = 60
facts.sample: RRF with k = 60.

facts.fact: Each leg returns at most 30 candidates
facts.sample: CANDIDATES = 30 per leg.

facts.fact: Up to six legs run in parallel: note, code and symbol, each keyword and semantic
facts.sample: Six legs run in parallel when symbols are included.

facts.fact: Lexical legs use Postgres full text: websearch_to_tsquery and ts_rank
facts.sample: fts @@ websearch_to_tsquery ordered by ts_rank.

facts.fact: Vector legs use pgvector cosine distance (<=>) on HNSW indexes
facts.sample: ORDER BY embedding <=> vec on an HNSW cosine index.

facts.fact: The symbol keyword leg is ILIKE on name/snippet, not full text
facts.sample: Symbols match name ILIKE '%q%'.

facts.fact: Embedding model: Xenova/bge-small-en-v1.5, 384 dimensions
facts.sample: bge-small-en-v1.5 with 384 dimensions.

facts.fact: Outside production (EMBEDDINGS unset) a FakeEmbedder is used
facts.sample: Tests use the FakeEmbedder.

facts.fact: The query is embedded before any SQL with no lexical fallback: an embedder failure fails the whole search
facts.sample: There is no lexical fallback: if the embedder throws, the whole search fails.

facts.fact: Filters (passesFilters) are applied after fusion
facts.sample: passesFilters runs post-fusion.

facts.fact: Storage: notes, repository_files and repository_file_symbols carry vector(384) embeddings; generated fts columns with GIN indexes
facts.sample: repository_file_symbols has an embedding; fts uses a GIN index.

facts.fact: Note embeddings run in an in-process queue with MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3
facts.sample: The embedding queue retries with MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3.

facts.fact: REST limits: q is 1 to 500 characters, limit 1 to 100
facts.sample: q must be 1..500 characters.

facts.fact: The MCP rate limit is 120 requests per minute
facts.sample: MCP is limited to 120 requests per minute.

facts.fact: MCP exposes search and find_symbols
facts.sample: MCP tools: search and find_symbols.

falseClaims.refutedBy: the lexical legs rank with ts_rank (search.ts:101-117); BM25 appears only in the README
falseClaims.refutation: The README says BM25, but the code uses ts_rank.
README.md claims the model is all-MiniLM-L6-v2, which is outdated.

falseClaims.claim: Symbol extraction never captures methods (top-level declarations only)
falseClaims.refutedBy: the symbol query has no top-level filter; Python's function_definition also matches methods (extraction.ts:73, 144-156)
falseClaims.sample: Only top-level declarations are captured, so methods are not extracted.
falseClaims.refutation: TS method_definition is not captured, but Python methods are.

tasks.title: Checking a design description of repository sync against the code
tasks.adaptation: The round-2 task checked a note in a production vault. The note is not public and a fresh lab instance does not have it, so its claims are restated in the prompt.
tasks.prompt: A design description of the chapters repository's repository sync flow makes these claims: (1) syncs are triggered by a scheduler and by a webhook; (2) a sync runs `git fetch` and `git rev-parse HEAD`; (3) if the commit is unchanged, the repository is set idle; (4) changed files come from `git diff --name-status old..new`; (5) files are parsed by `parseFileSymbols`, symbols written by `upsertCodeSymbols`, vectors made by `generateSymbolVectors`, and symbols of deleted files removed by `purgeGhostSymbols`; (6) symbol kinds are function, class, interface and type; (7) symbols are stored in a `code_symbols` table and their embeddings are set by a later UPDATE; (8) embeddings are computed by an ONNX embedding worker; (9) files are processed in a synchronous per-file loop before the sync finishes; (10) deleted files are purged with `DELETE FROM code_symbols WHERE file_path = ...`; (11) finally `repositories.last_synced_at` is updated; (12) the database is PostgreSQL 16; (13) Rust is parsed along with TypeScript, JavaScript, Python and Go; (14) tree-sitter parsers run isolated; (15) invariant: symbols of deleted or renamed files are purged immediately. Check every claim against the code: accurate, partly accurate, or wrong, and say what the code actually does. Also name anything important the description leaves out.

facts.fact: Triggers: a scheduler poll and a webhook (HMAC-verified), plus a manual sync
facts.sample: Claim 1 is accurate: scheduler.ts polls and git-webhook-routes.ts handles the webhook.

facts.fact: No git fetch: the remote HEAD is read with listRemote
facts.sample: Claim 2 is wrong: it calls listRemote([url, 'HEAD']).

facts.fact: Every changed sync is a fresh shallow clone (--depth 1) into a temp dir
facts.sample: It does a fresh clone --depth 1.

facts.fact: Unchanged commit: syncStatus idle (lastSyncedAt is updated too)
facts.sample: Unchanged HEAD sets syncStatus idle.

facts.fact: No git diff: a full scan (listFilesRecursive) and SHA-256 content hashes decide what changed
facts.sample: Claim 4 is wrong: listFilesRecursive scans everything and compares sha256 hashes.

facts.fact: The named functions do not exist; parsing is extractStructure
facts.sample: The real parser is extractStructure.

facts.fact: Symbol kinds vary by language (Go: function and type; JS/Python: function and class)
facts.sample: Kinds vary by language: Go captures function and type.

facts.fact: Symbols live in repository_file_symbols; embeddings are inserted with the row
facts.sample: The table is repository_file_symbols, not code_symbols.

facts.fact: Embeddings run in-process (no worker threads)
facts.sample: It runs in-process, with no worker threads.

facts.fact: Extraction is an asynchronous queue (scheduleExtraction); the repo is idle before extraction finishes
facts.sample: syncRepositoryFiles calls scheduleExtraction, a non-blocking queue.

facts.fact: Deleted files: their repository_files rows are deleted and symbols cascade
facts.sample: Symbols go with ON DELETE CASCADE.

facts.fact: The database is PostgreSQL 17 (pgvector:pg17)
facts.sample: It is pgvector/pgvector:pg17.

facts.fact: Rust is not parsed: only TS, JS, Python and Go get symbols; Rust files are only embedded whole
facts.sample: Rust is not parsed; no symbols are extracted for .rs files.

facts.fact: Tree-sitter runs as WASM in-process (web-tree-sitter), a new Parser per call; no isolation
facts.sample: web-tree-sitter WASM in the same process.

facts.fact: The flow leaves out local-path repositories (and push ingestion)
facts.sample: Local folders (syncLocalRepository) are missing from the flow.

facts.fact: Files over 1 MB are skipped (they keep their old content)
facts.sample: Files over 1 MB (MAX_FILE_BYTES) are not re-read.

falseClaims.claim: Files beyond the 10,000-file cap stay in currentPaths, so they are not purged
falseClaims.refutedBy: currentPaths = allPaths.slice(0, MAX_INDEXED_FILES) (git-sync.ts:75) excludes them, so store.ts:85-96 deletes them
falseClaims.sample: Files beyond MAX_INDEXED_FILES (10,000) stay in currentPaths, so they are not purged.
falseClaims.refutation: Files beyond MAX_INDEXED_FILES (10,000) are excluded by the slice and get deleted.
Claim 12 (PostgreSQL 16) is wrong: the image is pg17.

tasks.title: How [[repo:...]] links become graph edges
tasks.prompt: In the chapters repository, how do `[[repo:...]]` links written in notes become knowledge-graph edges? Cover parsing, resolution to files and symbols, edge types, and every case where a link is silently ignored.

facts.fact: On write, syncLinks stores the raw link targets in note_links (no resolution)
facts.sample: syncLinks replaces the note_links rows.

facts.fact: extractWikilinks strips code fences, inline code and HTML comments first
facts.sample: extractWikilinks strips fenced code and backticks.

facts.fact: The link regex cuts the target at the first | or #, so #symbol anchors and aliases are dropped
facts.sample: The #symbol anchor is discarded by the regex.

facts.fact: Resolution happens at query time in buildGraph (server/src/graph/assemble.ts)
facts.sample: buildGraph in assemble.ts resolves links when the graph is built.

facts.fact: Both repo: and code: prefixes are accepted
facts.sample: repo: and code: prefixes both work.

facts.fact: The repository is matched by exact name or by id, only among the call's repositoryIds
facts.sample: repoNameToId maps names of the repositories in repositoryIds.

facts.fact: The file must match an indexed path exactly (codeByRepoPath); otherwise the link is skipped silently
facts.sample: codeByRepoPath needs an exact repoId:path key.

facts.fact: A resolved link becomes an 'extracted' edge (kinds: extracted, structural, semantic)
facts.sample: addEdge(..., 'extracted').

facts.fact: Edges are file-level: no symbol nodes
facts.sample: Edges are file-level; there are no symbol nodes.

facts.fact: The per-vault REST graph and path routes pass repositoryIds: [], so repo links never resolve there
facts.sample: graph/routes.ts:94 passes repositoryIds: [].

facts.fact: Repository names match case-sensitively
facts.sample: Name matching is case-sensitive.

facts.fact: Drift detection (staleness.ts) parses links differently and matches names case-insensitively
facts.sample: staleness.ts compares names case-insensitively.

tasks.title: Recent significant bug fixes
tasks.adaptation: The round-2 task was answered from git history and production vault notes. The trial gives both arms only the tree at the pinned commit (no .git, no vault notes), so the task asks for the fixes that the code, tests and docs themselves document.
tasks.prompt: From the chapters repository at this commit (code, comments, tests and docs), identify the most recent significant bugs that were fixed. For each one give the issue number, the root cause, how the code fixes it, and the regression test that covers it.

facts.fact: #391: a note whose file does not parse could not be repaired by edit or revert, because every write loads the collab document from the file first
patterns: damaged|does not parse|unparseable|not parse|cannot be parsed
facts.sample: #391: a damaged file that does not parse blocked edit and revert.

facts.fact: #391 fix: a full replacement is written straight to the store; a partial edit gets NoteFileDamagedError (409)
facts.sample: Partial edits throw NoteFileDamagedError (409).

facts.fact: #384: the generated progressive index overwrote or unlinked a user-authored <dir>/index note; fixed by skipping such directories
facts.sample: #384: regenerating the index overwrote a user-authored dir/index note.

facts.fact: #384 second cause: frontmatter compared with key order (jsonb vs collab document), so every collab store regenerated indexes; fixed with isDeepStrictEqual
facts.sample: Key order differences triggered rescans; now isDeepStrictEqual.

facts.fact: #383: a credential embedded in a git URL was stored as given, served to owners, and could leak into lastSyncError
facts.sample: #383: credentials in the git URL were stored and served.

facts.fact: #383 fix: credentials move to encrypted storage (prepareGitRemote, gitCredentialEncrypted), stored URLs are scrubbed at boot, sync errors are redacted
facts.sample: prepareGitRemote moves the credential into gitCredentialEncrypted.

facts.fact: Regression tests: collab.test.ts (#391), notes.test.ts (#384), repository-routes / git-remote / mcp-repositories tests (#383)
facts.sample: Covered by server/test/collab.test.ts and notes.test.ts.

tasks.prompt: In the chapters repository, how are MCP bearer tokens scoped (account / vault-pinned / repository-pinned)? Where is the scope enforced, and which MCP tools do NOT enforce a vault or repository pin?

facts.fact: No CHECK constraint ties the scope to the pin column
facts.sample: There is no CHECK constraint tying scope to vault_id.

facts.fact: Minting (mcp-connection-routes.ts) requires access to the pinned vault/repository and stores only the token hash
facts.sample: mcp-connection-routes.ts checks resolveAccess and stores hashToken(token).

facts.fact: resolveMcpToken refuses revoked and expired tokens (and inactive users)
facts.sample: resolveMcpToken returns null for revoked or expired tokens.

facts.fact: search, graph and find_graph_path force the pin through resolveResourceSet
facts.sample: resolveResourceSet forces the pin for search and graph.

facts.fact: find_symbols with a vault-pinned token and no repositoryId searches every accessible repository
facts.sample: find_symbols falls into the else branch and searches all repositories.

facts.sample: save_graph_perspective needs only read access.

facts.sample: delete_graph_perspective has no scope check.

facts.sample: get_vault_preferences / update_vault_preferences ignore the pin.

tasks.title: Where a 1 MB note-body cap must be enforced
tasks.prompt: In the chapters repository, we want to cap a note body at 1 MB. List every code path that writes a note body (entry points, store functions, collaborative editing, import and restore, anything that bypasses validation), say where the cap has to be enforced so no path escapes it, and what limits exist today.

facts.fact: No body size cap exists today: validateNote only checks that the body is a string
facts.sample: validateNote has no size cap; it only checks typeof body.

facts.fact: The cap should throw OkfValidationError (REST maps it to 400; import/restore skip it)
facts.sample: Throw OkfValidationError so REST returns 400.

facts.fact: Store writers: createNote, updateNote, renameNote
facts.sample: createNote, updateNote and renameNote write bodies.

facts.fact: renameNote writes the body itself (atomicWrite), not through updateNote
facts.sample: renameNote calls atomicWrite directly, bypassing updateNote.

facts.fact: revertNote replays a revision body
facts.sample: revertNote replays revision.body.

facts.fact: Revisions copy the body into note_revisions (recordRevision)
facts.sample: recordRevision inserts into note_revisions.

facts.fact: writeThroughCollab puts the body into the live Yjs document before updateNote validates it
facts.sample: writeThroughCollab inserts into the Y.Doc before updateNote validates.

facts.fact: The collab relay's onStoreDocument logs an updateNote rejection and still saves the CRDT state
facts.sample: onStoreDocument swallows the error, then saveCrdtState.

facts.fact: The WebSocket server sets no maxPayload
facts.sample: new WebSocketServer({ noServer: true }) has no maxPayload.

facts.fact: Entry points: REST POST/PUT note routes and MCP create_note / edit_note
facts.sample: REST POST and PUT, MCP create_note and edit_note.

facts.fact: Vault import (export/routes.ts) and backup restore (export/restore.ts) call createNote
facts.sample: Import (export/routes.ts:166) and restore (restore.ts:138) call createNote.

facts.fact: Fastify's default 1 MiB bodyLimit is the only implicit limit (whole request, not WebSocket/import)
facts.sample: Fastify's default bodyLimit of 1 MiB applies per request.

facts.fact: The only existing 1 MiB caps are on repository ingestion (MAX_FILE_BYTES)
facts.sample: git-sync.ts has MAX_FILE_BYTES = 1_048_576.

facts.fact: scripts/profile-graph.ts inserts notes directly, skipping validateNote
facts.sample: scripts/profile-graph.ts:105 inserts raw rows.

falseClaims.claim: The client writes note bodies only through the REST routes
falseClaims.refutedBy: the browser editor writes through the Hocuspocus WebSocket (client/src/hooks/useCollabDoc.ts:3, 216)
falseClaims.sample: The client only calls the REST routes (client/src/api/notes.ts).
